claims.content: User
The PeaZip application must be installed and accessible on the computer system.
If initiating from within the application, the PeaZip file manager interface must be open.
If adding specific files or folders, the objects to be archived must exist and be selected in the file manager or operating system.

The user selects one or more files or folders in the file manager interface (or from the desktop) and initiates the archive creation process by clicking the 'Add' button, selecting 'Create archive' from the File menu, or choosing 'Add' from the context menu.

trigger.raw_text: The user selects one or more files or folders in the file manager interface (or from the desktop) and initiates the archive creation process by clicking the 'Add' button, selecting 'Create archive' from the File menu, or choosing 'Add' from the context menu.

claims.content: The user opens the 'Create archive' window by selecting 'Create archive' from the File menu, selecting 'Go to archiving layout' from the Browser menu, pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar after selecting objects, or using the context menu 'Add' option.
In the 'Create archive' interface, the user selects the desired compression format from the supported list and specifies the output storage space and archive name.
The user confirms the settings by clicking the 'Ok' button to generate the compressed archive.
The user may choose to split the archive content into multiple volumes of a defined size instead of creating a single volume archive.
The user may opt to append a timestamp to the created archive's name for backup purposes.
The user may set a password and optionally a keyfile to encrypt (lock) the created archive.
Instead of creating a new archive, the user may update an existing archive by adding extra objects (files or archives) to it.
A compressed archive file is created and saved at the user-specified output location with the defined name.
The created archive contains the selected files or folders, compressed to reduce storage space compared to the original input size.
The original source files or folders remain intact and are not deleted or modified on the computer system.
If encryption was configured, the created archive is locked and requires a password or keyfile for access.
If volume splitting was selected, the archive content is distributed across multiple volume files of the defined size.
